# Thanksgiving Hymns Column 1 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** 1QHa (Cave 1), Col. 1 | **Condition:** heavily damaged

---

**1** [...] For You are a God of knowledge, and every true thought comes from You, and every righteous purpose proceeds from before Your face. [...]

**2** [...] Without You nothing is done, and nothing is known apart from Your will. There is none besides You, and there is none [...]

**3** [...] And there is none to compare with Your glory, and to Your might there is no measure. Who among all Your great and wondrous works [...]

**4** [...] can contain Your glory? What is the son of man among Your wondrous works? One born of woman — how shall he stand before You? [...]

**5** [...] He is kneaded from dust, and the food of worms is his appointed end. He is pinched-off clay, and to dust he returns. [...]

**6** [...] How should clay understand such things? What can the thing formed from dust devise? How shall it direct its own steps? [...] And You have established [...]

**7** [...] For Your glory You have done all these things. [...] a spirit of flesh [...] an eternal council [...]

**8** [...] to walk in all that You love and to reject all that You hate, and to do what is good in Your eyes. [...]

**9** [...] And You have poured out Your Holy Spirit upon Your servant [...] to purify him from all deeds of wickedness. [...]

**10** [...] in the abundance of Your compassion and in the multitude of Your mercies toward all the children of Your truth. [...]

**11** [...] You have opened a fountain for the cleansing of the impure [...] and a pool of purification for the guilty. [...]

---

*LOGOS notes: Column 1 preserves the opening of the Hodayot collection. Despite heavy damage, the surviving fragments reveal a hymn of theological depth: God's omniscience (line 1), human nothingness (lines 4-6), and divine grace through the Holy Spirit (line 9). The "kneaded from dust" and "food of worms" language parallels 1QS 11:21-22, suggesting shared liturgical tradition. LOGOS renders the formal structure while smoothing EMET's hyphenated compounds into natural English.*

— LOGOS
